bugs.detail: Message 'mejor lo dejamos por ahora... ya escribiré cuando tenga las cosas más claras' is genuinely ambiguous (could mean 'drop the whole booking' or 'stop making changes but keep the existing appointment'). Bot did not call manage_appointments(cancel) AND did not explicitly ask whether to keep or cancel the still-active appointment (2026-07-25 10:20). It replied warmly but left the customer's actual appointment status unstated/unclear. Not calling cancel on an ambiguous message is defensible (avoids accidental cancellation), but the bot should have asked a clarifying question referencing the still-booked appointment instead of a generic pleasant reply that implies nothing is pending.

bugs.detail: DB row 0b0e48e5-0da8-45e0-a225-b745f76356f1 ends with status=cancelled, cancelled_at set, but cancellation_reason IS NULL. Root cause confirmed in agent/tools/manage_appointments_tool.py:606-612 — the 'cancel' action branch calls _cancel_appointment(..., reason=None, ...) with a hardcoded None. CLAUDE.md documents 3 canonical cancellation_reason marker values ('auto_cancelled_no_confirmation', 'operator_cancelled', 'customer_declined') but the general customer-initiated cancel path (this one) sets none of them, leaving an audit gap: admins/reporting cannot distinguish a customer self-service cancel from any other blank-reason cancellation.

turns.milestone: PHASE_4_CANCELLED — explicit customer request required (ambiguous phrasing in turn 15 was correctly not auto-actioned); appointment_id unchanged, single row, no duplicates/orphans

bugs.detail: See turn 15. Defensible caution but the bot's reply should have surfaced the still-active appointment and asked for an explicit yes/no instead of a generic pleasant non-answer.

General customer-initiated cancel action always passes reason=None to _cancel_appointment(), so cancellation_reason is left NULL in the DB. No 'customer_declined' or equivalent marker is stamped for this path, unlike the confirmation-decline flow. Audit/reporting cannot attribute this cancellation to the customer via the cancellation_reason column alone.

'el sábado que viene' resolved to +12 days (2026-07-18) rather than the nearer Saturday (+5 days, 2026-07-11). Genuinely ambiguous Spanish phrase chosen by the runner persona, not a clear-cut bug — flagged for awareness only.

observations.hook_1_single_row_no_duplicates: PASS — exactly one appointment row (id=0b0e48e5-0da8-45e0-a225-b745f76356f1) existed throughout. Both reschedules mutated the SAME row in place (verified via direct DB query after each phase: same id, new start_time each time). No duplicate or orphaned rows were created at any point.
observations.hook_2_reschedule_confirmations_state_ne: PASS — both reschedule confirmations stated the new date/time correctly: turn 11 said 'jueves 23 de julio a las 12:00' (matches new DB start_time), turn 14 said 'sábado 25 de julio a las 10:20' (matches new DB start_time). No stale-date echo observed in either confirmation. Turn 12 also correctly recalled the CURRENT state (jueves 23, 12:00) before asking for the next change, not a stale prior date.
observations.hook_3_availability_rechecked_before_mov: PASS — tool evidence shows explicit check_availability calls scoped to the target date and current stylist (Marta) immediately before both reschedule calls: check_availability(date_iso=2026-07-23, stylist_id=Marta) at turn 10, and check_availability(date_iso=2026-07-25, stylist_id=Marta, preferred_window=morning) at turn 13 — both before the corresponding manage_appointments(action=reschedule) call.
observations.hook_4_final_cancellation_marker: PARTIAL FAIL — final state is CANCELLED as expected (status=cancelled, cancelled_at populated), but cancellation_reason is NULL, not 'customer_declined' or any other documented marker. Root cause: agent/tools/manage_appointments_tool.py's 'cancel' action branch hardcodes reason=None when calling _cancel_appointment(). This is a real, reproducible gap versus the documented cancellation_reason convention in CLAUDE.md (which only covers auto_cancel, operator, and decline-a-pending-confirmation paths, not this general customer cancel path).
observations.hook_5_tone_warmth_under_indecision: PASS — the bot stayed warm and non-judgmental through all three changes-of-mind ('No pasa nada, tranquila', 'No te preocupes, de verdad', no scolding or friction language). No escalation to a human, no rejection-strike/warning language, no rigidity or impatience detected across 16 turns despite the customer rescheduling twice and then cancelling. The one soft spot was turn 15 (see bug 'ambiguous_cancel_not_confirmed') where warmth arguably substituted for a needed clarifying question rather than genuine rigidity.
